title: Protocol to combine brain sections from multiple mice into a single block for spatial transcriptomic analyses
author: Sei, Chaumeil, et al.
materials: Mouse monoclonal Anti-Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein Antibody, clone GA5 (1:100)Sigma-AldrichCat#MAB3402; RRID:AB_94844
Spatial gene expression slide: Example – Visium Spatial Gene Expression Kit10× GenomicsCAT#1000184
American Safety Razors Single Edge BladeFisher ScientificCAT#S04615

steps.title: Decontaminate hands and label samples
steps.instruction: Clean gloved hands with RNaseZap; assign a distinct colored permanent marker to the OCT of each of the four mouse brains. The entire assembly takes approximately 2 h.

steps.title: Position and trim brain ventrally
steps.instruction: Place the first brain in the cryostat with the ventral surface facing the blade; trim from the ventral side until the brainstem contacts the hypothalamus (midbrain flexure visible) in the same plane.

steps.title: Sagittal halve brain
steps.instruction: Using a single‑edge razor chilled in the cryostat, cut the brain straight down the midsagittal plane to produce left and right hemispheres.

steps.title: Remove halves and repeat for all brains
steps.instruction: Remove the two halves with a spatula or tweezers; repeat steps 1–3 for brains 2, 3, and 4.

steps.title: Mount selected halves on chucks
steps.instruction: Select one half of brain 1 and the matching half of brain 2; mount each on a separate cryostat chuck embedded in OCT with the midsagittal face up, trimming excess OCT with a single‑edge razor so the brain can be handled by the chuck.

steps.title: Align halves and warm faces
steps.instruction: Quickly align the two mounted halves by matching their midbrain flexures; briefly warm the sagittal faces by tapping each with a room‑temperature spatula pre‑treated with 70 % ethanol and RNaseZap until the OCT surface softens (brain remains frozen).

steps.title: Apply OCT and fuse halves (pair 1‑2)
steps.instruction: Apply a thin layer of OCT to the sagittal face of the brain 1 half, then firmly press the brain 2 half onto it, maintaining alignment of the midbrain flexure.

steps.title: Refreeze and detach merged pair
steps.instruction: Allow the OCT to refreeze in the cryostat, then remove the merged brain pair from each chuck one at a time.

steps.title: Merge brains 3‑4 using same procedure
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 5–8 with the selected halves of brains 3 and 4 to create a second merged pair.

steps.title: Remount merged pairs and expose ventricles
steps.instruction: Remount the merged 1‑2 block on the cryostat with the ventral surface facing the blade; shave the bottom face until two sets of ventricles become visible as white streaks.

steps.title: Horizontal cut to remove rostral block
steps.instruction: When ventricles are visible, make a horizontal incision with a single‑edge razor through both merged brains at the plane where thalamus meets striatum; discard the rostral portion of the block.

steps.title: Merge the two paired blocks
steps.instruction: Briefly warm the horizontal faces of the 1‑2 and 3‑4 merged blocks, apply a thin OCT layer, and press them together at the horizontal plane, holding only the mounting blocks to minimize tissue warming.

steps.title: Final coronal trim to reveal hippocampus
steps.instruction: Trim the coronal face of the fully assembled block until the hippocampus is visible in all four brains.

steps.title: Verify and refresh color coding
steps.instruction: Check that the colored markers applied in step 1 remain legible on the block sides; recolor any faded areas as needed.

steps.title: Optional storage of assembled block
steps.instruction: If storing, apply a thin coat of OCT on exposed brain areas, let it set, then place the block in a sealed container (e.g., a 50 mL conical tube) and freeze at –80 °C.

description: The protocol below describes specific steps for preparation of fresh-frozen mouse brains for use with spatial transcriptomic platforms. It is critical that institutional approval is obtained prior to work with live animals. This protocol uses the hippocampus as its region of focus. This protocol requires the use of a cryostat.
